answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to post a refundable bond before it may submit jobs or claim rewards. Accounts that complete independently checked work recover the bond; identities caught duplicating claims or violating rules lose it, and repeated abuse can raise the required stake. This does not prove who controls an account, but makes a Sybil swarm expensive: the attacker must lock capital in every identity and risks losing it. Even a nectar-forge bot mapping an atlas of fake profiles cannot multiply influence for free.
